prior_exception.reason: The defining 120 EC in years one and two is chemistry and laboratory centred: analytical, organic and inorganic chemistry; molecular structure and bonding; thermodynamics, quantum mechanics and physics; successive chemical synthesis and analysis laboratories. In year three, at least 12 EC of chemistry electives and a 12-EC independent chemistry research internship/report remain required. Although 27 EC can be freely chosen, UCR lacks a chemistry gateway and any stand-alone introductory or advanced organic, inorganic, analytical, physical or synthetic chemistry sequence. A 24-course UCR route using biology, geoscience, statistics and programming would have too little chemistry and would misrepresent the programme’s academic core.
prior_exception.curriculumContext: The official prospective year-one page is labelled 2027–28 while the year-two and year-three pages are indicative 2026–27; these are a present programme structure cross-check, not a guaranteed cohort contract. Year-three 9 EC taught compulsory work plus 12 EC compulsory internship plus 39 EC elective room = 60 EC; 12 of the latter is restricted to Chemistry electives, with 27 EC free. The education minor is optional, and alternative chemistry electives are not simultaneously required.
prior_exception.ucrCourseEvidence: Checked all 151 enriched UCR course rows, including descriptions, profile/topic enrichment, prerequisites and planned terms. HCBLIFE213 Biochemistry and HCBLIFE214 Life Science Laboratory provide biochemical content and molecular lab work, while HCBGATE101 and HCBLIFE211 introduce life science and cells. ENSENVI311 Environmental Biogeochemistry and ENSDELT311 R3: Recycling, Recovery, Remediation touch geochemical/inorganic processes and recovery; ENSSUST112 and ENSSUST211 address materials life cycles and energy systems. DISGATE102, DISMATH211/214/314 and DISGATE101 provide some mathematical, statistical and programming support. None provides the laboratory and theory progression in chemical analysis, organic/inorganic synthesis, physical chemistry, molecular spectroscopy and quantum chemistry required to underpin this bachelor and its independent chemistry research internship. Isolated biochemical and environmental chemistry coverage cannot support a defensible 24-course Chemistry match.

prior_exception.reason: Leiden is phasing in a revised Criminology curriculum. The current 2026-2027 Study Guide establishes the revised first and second years, but it expressly labels the displayed third year as the old curriculum for students who began in 2024 or earlier and states that Year 3 of the revised curriculum will only be published in the 2027-2028 guide. Combining the 120 EC revised sequence with the 60 EC legacy third year would create a pathway that no Fall 2026 entrant can follow. The missing applicable third-year structure cannot be inferred from the outgoing curriculum without inventing compulsory, elective, research and thesis requirements.
prior_exception.curriculumContext: The applicable revised curriculum is supported for 120 EC: 60 EC in Year 1 and 60 EC in Year 2, each composed of twelve compulsory 5-EC modules. It establishes integrated criminological theory, legal and criminal-justice study, psychological and sociological explanations, qualitative and quantitative methods, professional skills, policy evaluation, victims and offenders, cybercrime, investigation and prosecution, forensic psychology and experimental methods. The current product confirms that the programme as a whole is 180 EC, but the remaining revised 60 EC are not yet published. The legacy Year 3 shown in the same product is deliberately excluded because Leiden restricts it to earlier cohorts.
